findings.section: A lifecycle rule moves objects one way to colder classes and then expires them
findings.quote: 4. **Expire.** At the age you set, S3 deletes the object.
findings.evidence: Fact s3-lifecycle-expiration-versioned-delete-marker: "If the current object version is not a delete marker, Amazon S3 adds a delete marker with a unique version ID." and "Object expiration applies only to an object's current version (it has no impact on noncurrent object versions)." The chapter's own design turns versioning on (Decision record step 5: "Versioning keeps earlier versions, and a lifecycle rule moves older recordings to S3 Standard-IA"; STARTUP.md stage 1 adds S3 Versioning). So the startup example "deletes them after 7 years" only adds delete markers, and every recording stays stored and billed. The reader learns the wrong cause and effect for the one design she will explain. Fix: say that in a versioned bucket expiration adds a delete marker, and add NoncurrentVersionExpiration (fact s3-lifecycle-noncurrent-version-expiration) to the step and to the startup example.
findings.resolution: fix-21: same fix as technical-01 (versioned expiration adds a delete marker; NoncurrentVersionExpiration; startup example).

findings.section: Changed recently
findings.quote: > **Old:** set this way in the console, but not for buckets made with the API or AWS CloudFormation.
findings.evidence: "this way" has no antecedent in the box: the reader must guess which settings were set. The line also carries an open needs-display marker (lint W307, fact request fr-0048 for s3-change-bpa-acls-default-new-buckets-2023-04 "already console defaults"), so the old value is not yet a verified display (RULINGS hard rule 1). Fix: name the settings in the line once the display exists, for example "Old: Block Public Access on and ACLs off were already console defaults, ...".
findings.resolution: fix-21: the Old line names the settings: "until 2023-04-27, API and AWS CloudFormation buckets had Block Public Access off and ACLs on", linked; fr-0048 closed as withdrawn.

findings.section: Access points and Requester Pays control who reaches shared data and who pays
findings.quote: It can [accept requests only from a virtual private cloud](../facts/s3.md#s3-access-point-vpc-only).
findings.evidence: Fact s3-access-point-vpc-only: "you can also configure any access point to accept requests only from a virtual private cloud (VPC)". It is an option. The sentence reads as a limit of every access point ("can ... only"), and a skim reader concludes that every access point works only inside a VPC. Fix: "You can set an access point to accept requests only from one VPC."
findings.resolution: fix-21: "You can set one to accept requests only from a virtual private cloud."

findings.section: Intelligent-Tiering moves an unread object to cheaper tiers with no retrieval fee
findings.quote: Why no retrieval fee? The class charges a monitoring fee for each object instead, which makes it [the default storage class for virtually any workload](../facts/s3.md#s3-intelligent-tiering-ideal-for-unknown-access).
findings.evidence: The monitoring fee is not why AWS calls the class a default; the clause is a non sequitur. It also uses "default storage class" in a second sense: two subsections earlier, "Without a class in the request, [Amazon S3 assigns the S3 Standard storage class]" is the default. STYLE: one term per concept. Fix: "Why no retrieval fee? S3 charges a small monitoring fee for each object instead, so reads cost the same in every automatic tier." and drop or relabel the "default" phrase.
findings.resolution: fix-21: the "default storage class" phrase was removed from the Intelligent-Tiering Why line.

findings.section: A lifecycle rule moves objects one way to colder classes and then expires them
findings.quote: The move out of an archive class [can go only one way](../facts/s3.md#s3-lifecycle-no-transition-out-of-archive).
findings.evidence: The sentence says that a move out of an archive class exists and has a direction; the fact says a lifecycle rule cannot move an object back out. A second-language reader takes the literal meaning. Fix: "Transitions [can go only one way]: a rule never moves an object out of an archive class."
findings.resolution: fix-21: step 2 now reads "Objects move down a waterfall model ...: a rule never moves an object back to a warmer class."

findings.section: A lifecycle rule moves objects one way to colder classes and then expires them
findings.quote: No. One rule cannot move an object before its minimum duration ends, so the Deep Archive step needs [at least 94 days](../facts/s3.md#s3-lifecycle-no-single-rule-before-minimum-duration).
findings.evidence: Step 3 of the same subsection teaches the opposite impression: "an early move is [charged for the remainder of that duration]" (it is allowed, at a price). The Stop-and-answer then tests a rule the prose never states. Fact s3-lifecycle-no-single-rule-before-minimum-duration has both halves: "You can't create a single Lifecycle rule that transitions objects from one storage class to another before the minimum storage duration period has passed." and "You can specify two rules to accomplish this, but you pay the minimum duration storage charges." Fix: put both halves in step 3 (one rule: refused; two rules or a manual change: allowed and charged).
findings.resolution: fix-21: the Stop-and-answer now adds "Two rules can do it, but you pay that charge", which joins the one-rule limit with step 3 (s3-lifecycle-no-single-rule-before-minimum-duration).

findings.section: A presigned URL lends the permission of its signer until the URL expires
findings.quote: The URL [expires when the role session ends](../facts/s3.md#s3-presigned-url-expires-with-temporary-credentials), [typically 6 hours](../facts/s3.md#s3-presign-ec2-role-duration) for an instance role.
findings.evidence: A Spot the bug answer that names the cause but not the fix. READER.md: she must explain to customers and reason through unseen questions; a customer's next question is "so what do we do?". The chapter already has the answer in its own design (Decision record: the application signs a short-lived URL when the browser asks). Fix: add one sentence: sign a new URL each time the customer opens the link, instead of emailing a long-lived one.
findings.resolution: fix-21: Spot the bug answer adds "Sign a new short-lived URL each time the customer asks for the file."

findings.section: s3-t02 Share a private object with a presigned URL that expires
findings.quote: "trap": "s3-trap-presigned-url-own-permission"
findings.evidence: The trap s3-trap-presigned-url-own-permission is "A common belief is that a presigned URL carries its own permission" (2-deep.md). The only break-it step of s3-t02 shows expiry ("Wait until 2 minutes have passed since you created the URL. Reload the same browser tab."); no step signs with a principal that lacks s3:GetObject, so the task never touches the belief it claims to kill. Fix: set trap to null (the kills line about public buckets is what the task shows), or point the trap at expiry.
findings.resolution: fix-21: s3-t02 trap set to null; the task kills the public-bucket belief and shows expiry.

findings.section: s3-t03 Delete a versioned object and get it back
findings.quote: Fix it: copy the first version onto the same key, with the task tags. The copy becomes the current version of note.txt. Keep its version ID in V2.
findings.evidence: 2-deep.md step 5 of the versioning subsection says "To undelete, [you must delete this delete marker]" (fact s3-versioning-delete-the-delete-marker-restores: "To undelete the object, you must delete this delete marker."), and its Try it callout sends her to this task. The task fixes the delete by copying V1 instead and leaves the marker in place. With "must" in the prose and a different fix in the task, she cannot tell which one is right. Fix: make the fix step delete the marker by $MARKER (the mechanism the subsection teaches) and keep the copy-back as an optional second way, or soften the prose to "one way is ...".
findings.resolution: fix-21: same fix as technical-09: the task now undoes the delete by deleting the marker, as the prose teaches.

findings.section: Block Public Access overrides any policy or ACL that would make data public (and others)
findings.quote: **Stop and answer.** Block Public Access is on at the account level. One bucket has all four bucket-level settings off and a bucket policy that allows public reads. Can anyone on the internet read its objects?
findings.evidence: READER.md: "Headings, tables and captions must give a correct gist on their own; questions must test what the gist misses." From headings and tables alone I could answer this one (heading "Block Public Access overrides any policy...", level table "Applies to all buckets and access points"), the Object Lock one (1-fast table "Can the protection end early? ... No"), the Intelligent-Tiering one (heading "with no retrieval fee"), the Deep Archive eight-hours one (retrieval table) and Check 2 of 1-fast (table row "Needs a restore request first? ... Yes"). Only the versioning-suspended, atomic-write, Requester Pays and replication Stop-and-answers needed the prose. Fix: shift these to an edge the gist misses (for example, a bucket policy written before Block Public Access was turned on, or a legal hold after the retention date).
findings.resolution: deferred by fix-21: rewriting five Stop-and-answers toward edges the gist misses is an edit task; no word room in either file.

findings.section: How it works (all 14 subsections)
findings.quote: > **Say it:** The short answer is: a bucket in one Region holds objects by key. The thing to watch is that folders are key names.
findings.evidence: All 14 Say it lines use the same frame "The short answer is: ... The thing to watch is ...". Several are not sentences a customer would understand alone ("The thing to watch is who holds the link.", "The thing to watch is the bucket policy: it also decides."). READER.md asks for sentences she can say; one frame repeated 14 times trains a template, not an answer. Fix: vary the frame and make each line a complete thought that names the subject.

findings.section: Decision record
findings.quote: **Decision.** Presigned URLs: 15 minutes for an upload, 5 minutes for playback.
findings.evidence: The record lists three options but never says why the other two fail (random names are still public: fact s3-best-practice-wildcard-principal-means-anyone; all transfers through the instance load the instance with every byte). The trade-off also omits a consequence the chapter itself teaches: S3 checks the expiry "[at the time of the HTTP request]" (fact s3-presigned-url-reusable-until-expiry), so a player that sends a new request after 5 minutes (for example when the listener seeks in a long call) needs a new URL. Fix: one reason per rejected option, and one line on renewing the playback URL. Story values stay as STARTUP.md sets them.
findings.resolution: deferred by fix-21: same as technical-08 (word budget).

findings.section: A lifecycle rule moves objects one way to colder classes and then expires them; A single PUT stops at 5 GB so large uploads use multipart upload
findings.quote: Why one way? Lifecycle exists to lower cost as data ages.
findings.evidence: The "Why" line gives a purpose, not the mechanism (to warm data you restore a copy and write a new object, which a rule does not do). Same pattern in the multipart Stop-and-answer: "No. The files are below [5 GB]. Use multipart upload and Transfer Acceleration." names two fixes with no reason for either (a failed part is resent alone; the upload enters at a nearby edge location). Rule broken: the reader lens asks that a mechanism be explained as cause and effect, not only named.
findings.resolution: deferred by fix-21: cause-and-effect rewrites of the lifecycle Why line and the multipart answer did not fit the word budget.
